report.key-lede.say: Each <noun> below is laid out this way.

report.key-identifier.say: The standard's number and short name for the <noun>.

report.key-asked.say: The question we put to the <subject>, in italics.

report.key-answer.say: What we found in the <source>, and the reason for its status.

report.key-rests.say: The <where> on the grey bar, the quoted line beneath, and the strength of the evidence on the right. For something missing, the search we made, so anyone can repeat it.

report.key-looked.say: Each thing the standard looks for, numbered and marked found, missing, environment or does not apply. The status comes from how many were found. A scanner run during the review settled each item marked scanned, and its results are listed at the end.

report.key-status.say: Gap, Partial, Covered, Environment, Org-level or Not applicable, on the coloured tag. Not applicable means the system has none of what the question asks about. Org-level means the answer lies in what people or the organisation do, and no repository can show that. Environment means a technical control that can be set outside the repository, such as in the hosting platform, a cloud console or an identity provider, where this run saw nothing, so it isn't counted.

report.key-checked.say: Beside the model that read it: verified where a second check confirmed the answer against the <source>, and asserted where nothing did.

report.key-todo.say: The fix, on the orange bar. For <noun> the organisation owns, why the code can't answer it.

report.key-scope.say: The small tag after the name says whether the standard assesses this <noun> in every audit or only where the customer chooses it, and the words are explained below.

report.work-read.say: We read <whole> and answered <read> of the <total> <nouns> from <its> code and files. Each answer cites the lines it rests on, or, for something missing, the search that didn't find it.

say.one: The other <noun> is about how the organisation runs. A repository doesn't record that, so the report marks it for the organisation to answer.
say.many: The other <count> <nouns> are about how the organisation runs. A repository doesn't record that, so the report marks each one for the organisation to answer.

report.not-in-force.say: <title> isn't in force, so the pack answers it.

report.no-duty.say: <title> places no duty a repository could meet, so the pack answers it.

report.unsigned.say: Signature missing, document cannot be verified

report.signature-reason.say: Issued by Evalation. Any change after signing invalidates this signature.

report.org-runs.say: <title> is about how the organisation runs. A repository doesn't record that, so the report marks it for the organisation to answer.

report.org-records.say: <title> is kept in the organisation's own records. A repository doesn't hold them, so the report marks it for the organisation to answer.

report.work-untouched.say: We read the code without running it and changed nothing.

report.work-over-time.say: This review shows how each control is designed and whether the code puts it in place. An auditor checking that a control worked over a period of months also needs the records kept over those months.

report.repos-intro.say: We read these <count> repositories as one product, <name>. An answer can rest on evidence from any of them, and each citation names its repository. We mark an item missing only when none of them holds it.

report.repos-other.say: Other folders (not under version control). We read these for evidence too, and they have no commit history, so they aren't repositories.

report.slide-folder.say: Read for evidence, with no commit history.

report.scan-not-run.say: The <phase> didn't run over <here> this time.

report.scan-clean.say: The <phase> ran over <here> and found nothing <level>.

report.scan-clean-below.say: The <phase> ran over <here> and found nothing <level>, and <below> below that.

report.scan-listed.say: The scanner results at the end of this pack list each one.

report.label-organisation.say: Reason the code can't answer it

report.scanner-intro.say: Each card is a package or rule the scanners flagged, most severe first. An item counts only the severities it names, so a card can bear on an item without changing its result.

report.foot.say: <title>. Assessed on <date> against version <revision> of the questions.

report.foot-undated.say: <title>. Assessed against version <revision> of the questions.

report.check-unsigned.say: Not signed: this file carries no signature, so nobody can confirm Evalation issued it.

report.check-foreign.say: Altered: Evalation never issued the signed part of this file, so someone changed it or it came from elsewhere.

report.check-appended.say: Altered: Evalation issued this report on <date>, and someone added <bytes> bytes after signing, the way an editor saves a change.

report.check-genuine.say: Genuine: Evalation issued this report on <date>, and nothing has changed since.

report.left-clone.say: a second clone of <repository>, and the folder "<folder>" is read in its place

report.left-copy.say: a copy of the folder "<folder>" with no version control
